name: Lean physique looks taller

lead: Appearance forum users say that dropping body fat makes a person look taller by creating a longer, narrower silhouette, with the vertical line less broken by bulk at the waist and torso.

A narrower silhouette emphasises vertical length. Research on body shape covers attractiveness, such as waist-hip and waist-chest ratios (a waist-to-chest ratio has been reported as the largest determinant of male attractiveness), rather than perceived height; no studies were found on body fat and perceived height.

paras: People get there through fat loss with a calorie deficit and training, and keep muscle through the shoulders and back so the frame stays proportioned. Results build over the weeks or months it takes to lose fat.

Aggressive dieting and weight loss carry their own health risks, including nutrient shortfalls and loss of muscle. Individuals with a medical condition or history of disordered eating follow medical guidance.

angle.text: Losing body fat gives a longer, narrower silhouette, which appearance forum users say makes you look taller. Attractiveness research covers leanness and body shape in general; its effect on perceived height has not been studied.

lead: The claim that a lean physique makes a person look taller is common in appearance forums. Proponents say lower body fat creates a longer, narrower silhouette.

Research on body shape attractiveness, such as waist-hip and waist-chest ratios, addresses attractiveness rather than perceived height; a waist-to-chest ratio has been reported as the largest determinant of male attractiveness.[1]
No studies were found on body fat and perceived height.

paras: The waist-hip ratio is used as an indicator of health, and research on attractiveness has examined waist and chest ratios for men.[1] These findings do not address height perception.
